title: On‑Prem canary + fallback patterns and Terraform module guidelines
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a working playbook + implementation notes for safely delivering upgrades to on‑prem / VPC private deployments. Focus: CI/CD mechanics (Argo/ GitOps), Helm chart patterns, Terraform module interfaces, and image signing/attestation flow. The goal is pragmatic: reduce blast radius while keeping rollout velocity for customers running air‑gapped or VPC‑isolated clusters.

Design principles (short):
- Minimal cloud dependencies in customer-facing artifacts; CI runs in a build cluster, artifacts promoted via signed images/attestations.
- Playbookable signals (latency, error rate, pod restarts, custom healthchecks) drive automatic fallback.
- Terraform modules should be opinionated but composable: provide sensible outputs and hooks (lifecycle, locals, variables for policy enforcement).
- All image promotions require cryptographic signature (cosign) + attestation blob stored alongside the image.

Assumptions / prerequisites:
- Customer cluster runs ArgoCD (>=2.x) and supports Helm v3.8+.
- Build/CI can push images to a registry the customer allows and can optionally mirror into an airgapped pull-through mirror.
- There is a signing keypair managed by our KMS or customer HSM (for fully airgapped, customer supplies public key to verify signatures).
- Terraform state for private deployments is customer‑managed (S3/MinIO, GCS, Azure Blob).

High level pipeline (recommended):
1) CI builds image(s) and runs unit/integration/eval tests.
2) CI produces signed image + cosign attestation artifact.
3) CI opens a PR in the customer's GitOps repo (or our managed repo for dedicated customers) updating Helm chart image tags and generating a manifest change. PR includes attestation references.
4) ArgoCD picks up the PR (or merge) and runs a staged sync: canary subset -> canary validation -> progressive sync or failover to previous revision.

Canary strategy (practical):
- Define a "canary" subset via Helm values: replicaCount.canary, ingress/route weight, or dedicated Kubernetes label selectors.
- Default canary size = min(3, 5% of replicas, 1 node) — keep it small to reduce risk.
- Canary rollout phases: deploy -> readiness probes -> latency/error SLAs -> traffic ramp -> full sync. Each phase has timeouts and failure thresholds.

Signals and thresholds (examples):
- 5xx rate (app-level): fail if >1% for 3m on canary
- P95 latency: fail if >2x baseline for 3m
- CrashLoopBackOff: immediate fail
- Memory OOMs: immediate fail
- Custom smoke test: a scripted end-to-end request must succeed in <500ms for 3 consecutive checks

ArgoCD/Helm implementation notes:
- Use ArgoCD AppProject policies to restrict who can sync and which images can be referenced.
- Leverage ArgoCD sync waves/hooks for pre-sync (backup configmaps), sync (helm upgrade --install --wait), and post-sync (smoke tests).
- Example Helm values snippet for canary: 
  canary:
    enabled: true
    replicas: 2
    serviceWeight: 10  # percent
    healthCheckPath: /healthz

- Use Helm chart templates that support explicit subset labels: canary: true/false. Keep chart changes minimal: avoid surfacing experimental flags unless gated.

Terraform module guidelines (public interface):
- Module name: module.private_deploy.cluster (pattern)
- Variables (recommended):
  - cluster_name (string)
  - node_pools (list)
  - registry_mirror (string, optional)
  - argo_project (string)
  - enable_notary (bool)
  - attestation_public_key (string, optional)
  - ingress_controller (object)
- Outputs (required):
  - kubeconfig_path
  - argo_url
  - argocd_admin_secret_id
  - mirror_registry_endpoint
- Design note: keep signing-related variables optional to support both managed signing and customer-supplied keys.

Example terraform usage (pseudo):
module "private_cluster" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//private-cluster"
  cluster_name = "acme-prod"
  node_pools = [ {name="standard", size=3} ]
  enable_notary = true
  attestation_public_key = file("~/.keys/acme_pub.pem") 
}

Image signing and attestation flow (cosign recommended):
- CI step (after image build): cosign sign --key $KMS_URI image:tag
- Produce an in-toto/attestation predicate that lists artifacts (binary SHA, model SHA, eval run id, dataset snapshot id). Attach to the image registry as an OCI artifact.
- The GitOps PR references the signed tag and the attestation digest. ArgoCD pre-sync hook verifies signature using cosign verify --key $PUBLIC_KEY image:tag and validates the attestation if present.
- If verification fails, block sync and raise a failing status back to PR.

Key rotation / compromise handling (playbook):
1) Identify compromised key (monitor KMS audit logs).
2) Immediately mark new deployments as disallowed: set module variable attestation_public_key to new key only after rotation window.
3) Trigger a GitOps re-verify pass for recent merges (scan last 24h) to ensure images are signed with new key; reject merges signed with revoked keys.
4) For airgapped customers, coordinate offline key exchange and manual verification steps.

Preflight checks (CI / operator checklist):
- Helm template --validate on target chart with target values
- cosign verify against sample image
- TF plan should include no drift for argocd App resources
- Run smoke tests against staging cluster attached to the same overlay

Rollback and fast-fail strategies (runbook snippets):
- Automatic rollback: ArgoCD detects threshold breach -> triggers sync to previous healthy revision via automated rollback App operation.
- Manual fast rollback: run "argocd app rollback <app> --to-revision <rev>" or apply helm values set image.tag=<previous> and merge PR.
- For stateful components (DB migrations): require manual approval and patch-based schema migration (no automatic rollbacks).

Observability & verification (what to ship with):
- Per-app dashboard with: canary health, p95 latency, error_rate, pod restart count, memory/CPU OOMs.
- ArgoCD audit events and sync history retention for 30d.
- A small verification job that runs after full sync to run an end-to-end scenario and output structured results to S3/MinIO.

Failure modes and runbook (quick):
- Canary fails health checks: mark PR failing, revert image tag in git, notify SRE oncall, start rollback timer (T=0 start).
- Signature verification fails: block merge, notify security, require key re-registration flow.
- Partial region/network partition: If canary pods are healthy but network errors observed (>5% requests failing across nodes), pause rollout and escalate.

Open questions / TODOs (for next design pass):
- Partial traffic shaping: should we support weighted routing at LB level or prefer sidecar traffic shaping (consistency across customers)?
- Standardize attestation schema: propose a minimal JSON-LD predicate we expect for all images (model_version, eval_id, dataset_checksum, build_sha).
- How to best surface signature verification failures to customer's merge reviewers in a way that isn't noisy but actionable?

Appendix: quick CLI cheatsheet
- Build & sign (CI):
  docker build -t $REG/$REPO:$TAG .
  docker push $REG/$REPO:$TAG
  cosign sign --key $KMS_URI $REG/$REPO:$TAG
  cosign attest --key $KMS_URI --predicate=attestation.json $REG/$REPO:$TAG

- Verify locally: cosign verify --key ./public.pem $REG/$REPO:$TAG
- Trigger Argo re-sync (operator): argocd app sync my-app --retry-count 2 --revision HEAD

Notes to self (style / process):
- Keep the Terraform module small; encourage composability via outputs and example overlay repos.
- Document edgecases for airgap customers explicitly (manual attest exchange, offline verification scripts).
- Draft a condensed one‑pager for Sales that outlines SLA tradeoffs for automatic rollouts vs manual sign-offs.

References / links:
- Cosign docs: https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/
- ArgoCD hooks/health checks: https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io
- Internal GH PR with experimental attestation schema: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/pull/612

End of draft.

(Comments inline welcome — this is intentionally pragmatic and contains TODOs; aim to iterate with Solutions Eng and Security before we lock TF module v1.)
